Found and fixed while checkingThe Earth Engine land-cover rasters label everything outside the two 12 km circles as water (about 17,900 ha). That area is now masked; zone statistics use the circles only.
Footprint area differenceThe 0.4% gap against the source area attribute is uniform (5th to 95th percentile 0.995 to 0.997), so it is a different area calculation method, not a coordinate shift.
Not testable offlineAlignment against live basemap tiles. Overlays are placed in the same Web Mercator grid the tiles use, and registration against the source raster is tested above; check the port marker against OSM when you open the file.
Validation: land cover vs mangrove map94% of the CGMD 2023 mangrove pixels are labelled flooded vegetation (69%) or trees (25%) by Dynamic World 2023.
Validation: built-up land vs building footprints82% of footprint centres lie within 30 m of smoothed built-up land 2023 (7% for random land pixels); 57% of the built-up land lies within 30 m of a footprint, the rest being paving, bare ground or unmapped buildings.
Validation: dating of changeFor 7,319 footprints dated 2017–2023 that sit on or beside smoothed built-up land, the first year of footprint detection and the year built-up land first appears differ by 1 year at the median, and 68% agree within 2 years (rank correlation 0.27). Read years of change as ±2 years. The two series of cumulative dated buildings and built-up hectares, 2017–2023, correlate at 0.93.
Validation: area and distance arithmeticAreas are counted on 10 m UTM pixels; straight-line distances in UTM differ from geodesic distances by at most 0.04% on every point layer, and the study circles measure 12,000 m geodesically.
Corrected during validationThe 2017 built-up total first left out about 9 ha of pixels with no data in the 2017 composite although the smoothing also uses 2018 and 2019; including them makes the baseline 1,040 ha and the growth to 2026 +76% instead of +78%.

Land cover: Dynamic World 10 m, Jan–Sep composites; the map layer is shown at 20 m. Built-up land is smoothed with a 3-year majority so one-year classifier swings are not read as change; the first two years (2017–18) and last two (2025–26) cannot be told apart by this method. Against the footprint dating, 68% of years agree within two years, so treat years of change as plus or minus two years. Buildings: Google Open Buildings footprints (2023), dated by the Open Buildings temporal raster ("2016" means present by 2016; 2024 onward is not covered). Port site: the village of Kililana, Manda Bay (county database), the best documented position for Lamu Port; confirm it against the basemap.
